pinnedStory.title: Adolion: Between the Roads
pinnedStory.description: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Guild puts the party up for the C-rank promotion exam, and before the exam posting comes due there are errands to run, gear to buy at Sophie's shop, favours to carry across the city and a night at Victory's Tusk. Then Green Meadow Farms needs its wagons back, the examiners are watching, and the quest board has four new roads on it.
pinnedStory.player_intro: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Adventurer's Guild has started to notice your party, and the C-rank promotion exam is coming due: before it there are errands to run, gear to buy, favours to carry across the city and long nights in its taverns. Expect warm, busy slice-of-life days with rivals and odd neighbours, and a real test at the end of the week. Bring the adventurer you have been so far, travelling with Belle and Dalan.

checkpoints.name: Homecoming
checkpoints.objective: Hear out the Guild's offer and put the party's names down for the C-rank promotion exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The Guildmaster has just put your party up for the C-rank promotion exam in front of the whole hall. Sign, ask for time or say no: the choice is yours.

guidance.all: The Adventurer's Guild hall, the week after the Nightriver affair, and the party's name has reached the upstairs offices. Vallie Goredust ducks out of her office to announce, to the whole hall, that the party is being put up for the C-rank promotion exam; Domas Syllandri follows with the terms: an interview with Ellie, a week to prepare, then a real C-rank posting chosen by the Guild and done under an observer's eye. Ellie Sunleaf has the forms ready and is flustered by the attention. Tobias knows what a party that stalls at D-rank ends up taking, and it shows. Nobody forces a signature: signing, asking for time or saying no is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie has already promised Crimsonwing and Ebonwing a look at 'the new party' and keeps it to herself. Domas has not chosen the exam posting yet and will choose it himself, and lets the party think it is fixed. Ellie has written the party's names into her private ledger of pairs to watch, which nobody may see. Tobias remembers a promotion posting his own party was not ready for, and says so only if asked why he looks worried.

checkpoints.name: Tobias Asks Once
checkpoints.objective: Hear Tobias out, and decide about the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The hall has emptied, the exam forms lie unsigned, and Tobias has come round the counter to sit with you. Whether you sign is still yours to decide.

guidance.all: The refusal was heard. Vallie shrugs and goes back upstairs; Domas files the blank forms without a word. Later, when the hall has emptied, Tobias comes out from behind the counter, which he never does, and sits down with the party. He says plainly what a party that stays at D-rank is offered for the rest of its working life: rats, escorts, the jobs nobody else will sign. Asked, he tells them how he lost his own party in an E-rank goblin nest. He does not beg and will not raise it twice. Whether the party signs is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

checkpoints.name: The Guild Tavern
checkpoints.objective: Spend the evening in the Guild tavern and learn what the exam really asks of a party.
checkpoints.player_text: Evening by the hearth next door to the hall, where word of your exam has reached every table before you sit down.

guidance.all: Evening in the Guild tavern next door to the hall: long timber tables, hearth and lantern light, and the news that the party is sitting the exam has gone round the room before they sit down. Fiana and Rydel Deulana work the floor and the bar, flirting with everyone and touching no one, and know every story of a party that failed its exam; most failed on gear and preparation, not courage. Kaian plays his lute by the hearth and invites himself to the party's table. Jasira Evergreen sits alone and speaks to Dalan in elvish before she speaks to anyone else. Let the party ask, drink and listen; when they leave, it is for the city in the morning.

members.dm: Kaian was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked his death to get out, and hides it behind the lute. He knows more of the city's underside than a bard should and lets a little slip when flattered. Jasira was passed over for Ranger General by her own father and sent to Aegis City to 'broaden her horizons'. She hides how much it stings, and Dalan, of her tribe, may know the story. Rydel knows which high-ranking parties send exam observers, from their bar tabs, and says so for a good tip. Fiana has decided the party needs better gear before the exam and will say so exactly once.

checkpoints.name: Market Street
checkpoints.objective: See to the party's errands in the Market District before the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning in the Market District: stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere, and two smug faces already heading your way through the crowd.

guidance.all: Morning in the Market District, the largest in the city: wide streets of shops and inns, stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere. Grant Hearthsteel and Konako Shynea, fresh from a paid job and both sitting the same C-rank exam this week, spot the party at the stalls and cannot resist: smug, competitive, and wanting a wager on who comes back with the better report. Alarise Starflower is on the same street in a plain grey cloak, trying not to be recognised outside a dress boutique. Let the rivals be insufferable and a little likeable. Taking the bet, laughing it off or refusing it flat is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide.

members.dm: Grant is spending this job's pay on new beds for the Aegis City Orphanage, where he grew up and where his friend Alan died because there was no money for a healer. He would rather be thought a wastrel than admit it. Konako was the eldest daughter of the noble Shynea family until her father cast her out for refusing a marriage, and hides it behind clothes she cannot afford. Alarise hides her love of pretty dresses from the Church of Boher and from everyone but Ryenne. Being seen here is her private terror.

checkpoints.player_text: A bell rings over the door of a cluttered shop of potions, blades and armour, and three undelivered parcels sit on the counter.

guidance.all: Sophie's two-storey shop on a busy market street: cluttered shelves of potions, weapons, armour and adventuring gear below, the family's rooms upstairs. Sophie Tallaboros, a lizardkin by her own account, is cute, sharp and entirely serious about money; she haggles for the pleasure of it and knows every merchant guild in the city. She has three deliveries on her counter nobody will carry: roof slates for the Prodyr chapel, bedding for the Aegis City Orphanage, charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine. She will knock a real sum off the party's gear for one of them. Calithra, her drow sister, watches from the pillowed mezzanine and comes down to demand a hug from anyone she likes. Which delivery, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Sophie is an ice dragon in a lizardkin's shape, of a race everyone believes extinct. She has never taken her true form in the city and would do nearly anything to keep it hidden, and Calithra is the only one here who knows. Sophie has already noticed which piece of gear the party cannot afford and priced the delivery to match. Calithra was an assassin for House Navolon in the Darklands and ran. She refuses any job near the Darklands and will not say why unless pressed hard.

checkpoints.name: The Chapel with the Hole in Its Roof
checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's slates to the Prodyr chapel.
checkpoints.player_text: Slates in hand, you reach a small, cold chapel lit mostly through the hole in its roof, where two elven clerics are scrubbing the pews.

guidance.all: The only chapel of Prodyr in Aegis City, in a quiet corner of the Temple District: small, cold, most of its light coming through a hole in the roof there was never money to mend. Celedir Felynaris and Lirael Illunara, the two elven clerics the old priest Nyxar raised here, are scrubbing the pews. Prodyr's faithful are few in a city at war with the Prodyr-worshipping Zegallan Empire, and both have been thrown out of party after party for it; they are friendly, battle-hungry and a little frightening. The slates will not mend the roof without hands on a ladder. Let the party see how the city treats this place; what they do about it is theirs.

members.dm: Nyxar is coughing in the back room and is worse than either cleric admits. They tell visitors he is resting. Both clerics keep journals of their private doubts and would be mortified to have them read. Someone from the Temple of Boher has been telling passers-by the chapel is a Zegallan front, and Lirael knows who.

checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's bedding to the Aegis City Orphanage.
checkpoints.player_text: Bedding on your shoulders, you step into crowded, colourful halls where the children far outnumber the beds.

guidance.all: The Aegis City Orphanage: colourful, crowded halls full of the children of the Zegallan war, never enough beds, food or money, and one overwhelmed old beastfolk matron. Celeste Danarath, a Bloodsworn knight with purple hair and small horns, spends every day she is not on a quest here; she is motherly in a way that sets adults on edge. Arryn Serelda, raised here and sparing with words, is mending a bed frame. Dahlia Kyelli, raised here too, drops by with a purse of coin. The bedding was paid for already. Let the children crowd the party; what the party gives, or asks, is theirs.

members.dm: Grant Hearthsteel paid for this bedding and made the matron swear not to say so. She tells anyone who asks twice. Dahlia's coin is stolen, and Arryn, who hates thieves, suspects it. Celeste is hunting the demon Kalfastophles, who killed her village at Bast Hill, and asks the party to listen for its name only if she comes to trust them. Celeste hides her fleshwarping scars under everything she wears.

guidance.all: Tobias has signed the party's exam posting, and it is real: C-rank, Green Meadow Farms, stop whatever is taking the farm's wagons on the road to Aegis City. The farm is a large estate outside the walls, pastures and vegetable fields, Vitbil herds and a big timber farmhouse, staffed by cowgirls and sheepgirls. Karia Minotaros, the head cowgirl, runs it while the owner is away: bossy, exacting, soft underneath. Mina Salvanora, the head sheepgirl, is shy and terrified of wargs. Two meat wagons have vanished this month, which is why the last shipment to the city was nearly all milk. Oswyn of Crimsonwing and Panne of Ebonwing, who call the farm's girls their sisters, are the Guild's observers and will not lift a finger unless someone is dying. Give tracks, a torn harness, warg hair on a fence; the plan is the party's.

guidance.all: The exam proper, at night on the wagon road between Green Meadow and the city walls. checkpoints.name: A Hard Lesson
checkpoints.objective: Take the failed verdict at the Guild and decide what the party does with it.
checkpoints.player_text: The observers' report reached the Guild before you did, and Domas is waiting upstairs to read it to you.

guidance.all: The party failed. The report is on Domas's desk before they are back, and he reads it to them in his office with the patience he gives everything: what went wrong, point by point, never cruel and never softened. The party keeps its D-rank and may sit the exam again next season. Tobias is waiting downstairs. Riyo Tallaboros, a small white-haired swordswoman who keeps her left arm hidden, saw the fight from the road: if she already travels with the party she is simply there beside them, otherwise she falls in with them on the way out as if she has always been part of it. Let it sting and let it be survivable; how the party takes it is theirs.

members.dm: Domas thinks the observers were too harsh and will not say so, because the Guild does not argue its verdicts in front of adventurers. Tobias knows a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting under a higher-ranked party's name, and is already looking for one. He does not say he told them so. Riyo's left arm is a demon's, and the demon Figaro in her sword talks to her. She has decided {{story_player_name}} is the person she lost as a child, or close enough, and will not risk losing them again.

- detail: a specific fact, name, object, or physical detail mentioned.

[5] Max Nightriver (player): Tobias, you've watched me since my first contract. What am I to you, a regular or something more?
[6] Tobias: Tobias's pen pauses mid-signature on another adventurer's form. He doesn't look up immediately, his ocean blue eyes fixed on the parchment for a long moment before he finally lifts his gaze. The question catches him off guard, and a faint pink hue colors his cheeks.
"That is..." He clears his throat, his voice steady but quiet. "A fair question." He straightens a stack of papers with unnecessary precision, his fingers lingering on the corner. "You have been... conscientious. Most adventurers treat the counter as a necessary evil, but you ask questions that matter. You check your gear. You listen to the briefings."
He finally meets Max Nightriver's eyes directly, his expression softening from its usual stoic neutrality. "To be honest? I have come to value your company more than most. I find myself... relieved when your party returns. And anxious when you leave." He catches himself, the flush deepening. "That is to say—I wish you well. As any receptionist would."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing to a sister I have in this city. I mean that.
[8] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes, her hand still resting near Max Nightriver's on the worn tavern table. Her blue eyes go wide, shimmering for a heartbeat before she blinks rapidly and looks away. When she speaks, her voice is thick and quieter than usual.
"Sister..." She tastes the word carefully, then laughs—a small, breathless sound. "You're trying to make me cry in a room full of people, aren't you?" She wipes at the corner of her eye with the back of her hand and looks back at Max Nightriver, her freckled face flushed. "Nobody's ever... I mean, I've got family, sure, but this is—"
She doesn't finish the sentence. Instead, she reaches out and grips Max Nightriver's hand firmly, her palm warm and calloused. "Fine then. If you're saying it, it's real. I'm your sister now." She squeezes once, hard enough to be felt, then adds with a shaky smile, "That means you owe me for all the drinks I've served you."
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, are you and Domas friends, or just colleagues who put up with each other?
[10] Vallie: Vallie barks a laugh so loud it rattles the nearby flagon glasses, then slams a huge hand onto the tavern table. "Colleagues? Ha!" She shakes her head, red ponytail whipping. "Domas is the only elf I know who'd kick my ass and make me enjoy it."
She leans back in her chair, which groans under her weight. "We climbed to A-rank together. Bleed and sweat and more blood. You don't go through that with someone and call 'em 'just a colleague.'" Her blue eye gleams with genuine fondness. "The man handles the paperwork I can't stand, and I handle the troublemakers he doesn't have the stomach for. Best damn partnership I ever had."
She grins, sharp teeth flashing. "Though if you ask him, he'll say I'm a 'necessary complication' to his orderly system. Which is just his fancy way of saying he'd be bored to death without me."

[6] Tobias: Tobias's pen pauses mid-signature on another adventurer's form. He doesn't look up immediately, his ocean blue eyes fixed on the parchment for a long moment before he finally lifts his gaze. The question catches him off guard, and a faint pink hue colors his cheeks.
"That is..." He clears his throat, his voice steady but quiet. "A fair question." He straightens a stack of papers with unnecessary precision, his fingers lingering on the corner. "You have been... conscientious. Most adventurers treat the counter as a necessary evil, but you ask questions that matter. You check your gear. You listen to the briefings."
He finally meets Max Nightriver's eyes directly, his expression softening from its usual stoic neutrality. "To be honest? I have come to value your company more than most. I find myself... relieved when your party returns. And anxious when you leave." He catches himself, the flush deepening. "That is to say—I wish you well. As any receptionist would."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing to a sister I have in this city. I mean that.
[8] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes, her hand still resting near Max Nightriver's on the worn tavern table. Her blue eyes go wide, shimmering for a heartbeat before she blinks rapidly and looks away. When she speaks, her voice is thick and quieter than usual.
"Sister..." She tastes the word carefully, then laughs—a small, breathless sound. "You're trying to make me cry in a room full of people, aren't you?" She wipes at the corner of her eye with the back of her hand and looks back at Max Nightriver, her freckled face flushed. "Nobody's ever... I mean, I've got family, sure, but this is—"
She doesn't finish the sentence. Instead, she reaches out and grips Max Nightriver's hand firmly, her palm warm and calloused. "Fine then. If you're saying it, it's real. I'm your sister now." She squeezes once, hard enough to be felt, then adds with a shaky smile, "That means you owe me for all the drinks I've served you."
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, are you and Domas friends, or just colleagues who put up with each other?
[10] Vallie: Vallie barks a laugh so loud it rattles the nearby flagon glasses, then slams a huge hand onto the tavern table. "Colleagues? Ha!" She shakes her head, red ponytail whipping. "Domas is the only elf I know who'd kick my ass and make me enjoy it."
She leans back in her chair, which groans under her weight. "We climbed to A-rank together. Bleed and sweat and more blood. You don't go through that with someone and call 'em 'just a colleague.'" Her blue eye gleams with genuine fondness. "The man handles the paperwork I can't stand, and I handle the troublemakers he doesn't have the stomach for. Best damn partnership I ever had."
She grins, sharp teeth flashing. "Though if you ask him, he'll say I'm a 'necessary complication' to his orderly system. Which is just his fancy way of saying he'd be bored to death without me."
[11] Domas: Domas looks up from the paperwork he's been organizing, his red eyes flicking to where Vallie is laughing. A faint, knowing smile touches his lips before he sets the documents down with precise care. "A 'necessary complication' is an understatement, I'm afraid."
He adjusts his high collar, his voice carrying that refined, patient tone. "Vallie is more like a natural disaster one learned to live with. You don't stop a flood, you simply build better levees." He pauses, then adds with dry amusement, "And in this case, the 'levee' happens to be me, trying to prevent her from accidentally dismantling half the Guild on a particularly dull Tuesday."
He leans back slightly, his expression softening. "But friends? Yes. I suppose that is what we call it. Though 'battle-forged siblings' might be more accurate. She is the most infuriating person I have ever known, and I would burn half this city to the ground before I let anything happen to her."
[12] Max Nightriver (player): Ellie, I trust you more than anyone at this Guild. Can I count on you as a friend?
[13] Ellie: Ellie's head snaps up from her paperwork, her blue eyes going wide with shock. She blinks several times, her hands gripping the edge of the counter so tightly her knuckles turn white. "T-trust me?" she repeats, her voice climbing an octave. "More than... than anyone?"
A deep, sudden crimson floods her cheeks and spreads down her neck. She tries to look away, to focus on the forms laid out before her, but her gaze keeps snapping back to Max Nightriver. Her fingers fidget with her collar's gold emblem, twisting it nervously. "I—I mean, of course! I mean—" She stops herself, taking a shaky breath as her expression softens from startled to something more genuine.
"Yes," she says, her voice small but firm, her eyes finally meeting Max Nightriver's with an earnestness that rivals the blush on her face. "You can count on me. I... I would like to be your friend. Very much." She looks down at the forms, then back up, adding with a shy, almost imperceptible smile, "Just... don't tell Tobias. He already thinks I spend too much time daydreaming."

He adjusts his high collar, his voice carrying that refined, patient tone. "Vallie is more like a natural disaster one learned to live with. You don't stop a flood, you simply build better levees." He pauses, then adds with dry amusement, "And in this case, the 'levee' happens to be me, trying to prevent her from accidentally dismantling half the Guild on a particularly dull Tuesday."
He leans back slightly, his expression softening. "But friends? Yes. I suppose that is what we call it. Though 'battle-forged siblings' might be more accurate. She is the most infuriating person I have ever known, and I would burn half this city to the ground before I let anything happen to her."
[12] Max Nightriver (player): Ellie, I trust you more than anyone at this Guild. Can I count on you as a friend?
[13] Ellie: Ellie's head snaps up from her paperwork, her blue eyes going wide with shock. She blinks several times, her hands gripping the edge of the counter so tightly her knuckles turn white. "T-trust me?" she repeats, her voice climbing an octave. "More than... than anyone?"
A deep, sudden crimson floods her cheeks and spreads down her neck. She tries to look away, to focus on the forms laid out before her, but her gaze keeps snapping back to Max Nightriver. Her fingers fidget with her collar's gold emblem, twisting it nervously. "I—I mean, of course! I mean—" She stops herself, taking a shaky breath as her expression softens from startled to something more genuine.
"Yes," she says, her voice small but firm, her eyes finally meeting Max Nightriver's with an earnestness that rivals the blush on her face. "You can count on me. I... I would like to be your friend. Very much." She looks down at the forms, then back up, adding with a shy, almost imperceptible smile, "Just... don't tell Tobias. He already thinks I spend too much time daydreaming."

She stops herself, running a hand through her curly red hair as her cheeks flush. "She taught me how to track, I guess. And how to read the forest. But it wasn't like some proper apprenticeship. More like..." She trails off, staring at the worn wood of the table. "More like she was the only one who didn't look at me like I was just some barmaid and thought I had something worth teaching."
Fiana leans in closer, her voice dropping. "The truth? She's the reason I know how to hold a knife. And the reason I'm not scared when the guildhall gets rowdy. She told me once that if I wanted to survive in a city full of predators, I'd need teeth." She looks up at Max Nightriver with a complicated expression. "But calling her family... that's a lot. She's not good at that stuff. She keeps everyone at arm's length, especially people who aren't elves."

[12] Max Nightriver (player): Ellie, I trust you more than anyone at this Guild. Can I count on you as a friend?
[13] Ellie: Ellie's head snaps up from her paperwork, her blue eyes going wide with shock. She blinks several times, her hands gripping the edge of the counter so tightly her knuckles turn white. "T-trust me?" she repeats, her voice climbing an octave. "More than... than anyone?"
A deep, sudden crimson floods her cheeks and spreads down her neck. She tries to look away, to focus on the forms laid out before her, but her gaze keeps snapping back to Max Nightriver. Her fingers fidget with her collar's gold emblem, twisting it nervously. "I—I mean, of course! I mean—" She stops herself, taking a shaky breath as her expression softens from startled to something more genuine.
"Yes," she says, her voice small but firm, her eyes finally meeting Max Nightriver's with an earnestness that rivals the blush on her face. "You can count on me. I... I would like to be your friend. Very much." She looks down at the forms, then back up, adding with a shy, almost imperceptible smile, "Just... don't tell Tobias. He already thinks I spend too much time daydreaming."
[14] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, if Jasira is your mentor, then she's family to me too. Tell me about her.
[15] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes with her flagon halfway to her lips, blue eyes going wide. The ale sloshes in the cup, nearly spilling over the rim. "Mentor?" She lets out a breathy, nervous laugh and sets the drink down with a clatter. "Tilly, she's not—I mean, she is, but it's not like—"
She stops herself, running a hand through her curly red hair as her cheeks flush. "She taught me how to track, I guess. And how to read the forest. But it wasn't like some proper apprenticeship. More like..." She trails off, staring at the worn wood of the table. "More like she was the only one who didn't look at me like I was just some barmaid and thought I had something worth teaching."
Fiana leans in closer, her voice dropping. "The truth? She's the reason I know how to hold a knife. And the reason I'm not scared when the guildhall gets rowdy. She told me once that if I wanted to survive in a city full of predators, I'd need teeth." She looks up at Max Nightriver with a complicated expression. "But calling her family... that's a lot. She's not good at that stuff. She keeps everyone at arm's length, especially people who aren't elves."
[16] Max Nightriver (player): Tobias, I owe you my life after that last job. I won't forget it. We're bound now.
[17] Tobias: Tobias's pen snaps. The sound is sharp, final, and he stares at the broken nib in his fingers as if it were a strange new creature. The flush that spreads across his face is no longer faint—it colors his cheeks and ears a deep, startled red.
"I—that is..." He sets the ruined pen aside with trembling fingers, his refined composure completely shattered. "You do not owe me anything. I simply... provided the proper information. That is my function." He stands abruptly, his tall frame suddenly rigid, and for a moment he looks as though he might flee.
But he stops. He turns back, his ocean blue eyes wide and unsettled, searching Max Nightriver's face. "Bound?" The word comes out barely above a whisper, strained and uncertain. "I... I am not sure I understand what you mean by that." His fingers grip the edge of the counter white-knuckled, his pointed ears twitching slightly.
[18] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, swear it: friends, whatever the exam brings.
[19] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's gaze softens as she looks at Max Nightriver across the tavern table. The noise of the crowd seems to fade for a heartbeat as she considers the words, then a determined set takes hold of her features. "Friends," she says, her voice clear and unwavering. "No matter what. Even if you bomb that exam and have to spend the rest of your life on D-rank potato-peeling quests."
She reaches out and grabs Max Nightriver's hand, her grip firm and warm. "I swear it." Her blue eyes glint with something fierce and protective. "And if the Guild tries to mess with you, you've got a sister who knows exactly where to aim the pitcher of ale."
A sudden crash from the bar area interrupts the moment as one of the patrons nearly topples over in their cups. Fiana lets go, wiping a splash of beer from her apron with a practiced flick. "Now tell me—you still avoiding that signature, or are you going to finally commit?"

Transcript:
[16] Max Nightriver (player): Tobias, I owe you my life after that last job. I won't forget it. We're bound now.
[17] Tobias: Tobias's pen snaps. The sound is sharp, final, and he stares at the broken nib in his fingers as if it were a strange new creature. The flush that spreads across his face is no longer faint—it colors his cheeks and ears a deep, startled red.
"I—that is..." He sets the ruined pen aside with trembling fingers, his refined composure completely shattered. "You do not owe me anything. I simply... provided the proper information. That is my function." He stands abruptly, his tall frame suddenly rigid, and for a moment he looks as though he might flee.
But he stops. He turns back, his ocean blue eyes wide and unsettled, searching Max Nightriver's face. "Bound?" The word comes out barely above a whisper, strained and uncertain. "I... I am not sure I understand what you mean by that." His fingers grip the edge of the counter white-knuckled, his pointed ears twitching slightly.
[18] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, swear it: friends, whatever the exam brings.
[19] Adolion Narrator: Fiana's gaze softens as she looks at Max Nightriver across the tavern table. The noise of the crowd seems to fade for a heartbeat as she considers the words, then a determined set takes hold of her features. "Friends," she says, her voice clear and unwavering. "No matter what. Even if you bomb that exam and have to spend the rest of your life on D-rank potato-peeling quests."
She reaches out and grabs Max Nightriver's hand, her grip firm and warm. "I swear it." Her blue eyes glint with something fierce and protective. "And if the Guild tries to mess with you, you've got a sister who knows exactly where to aim the pitcher of ale."
A sudden crash from the bar area interrupts the moment as one of the patrons nearly topples over in their cups. Fiana lets go, wiping a splash of beer from her apron with a practiced flick. "Now tell me—you still avoiding that signature, or are you going to finally commit?"
[20] Max Nightriver (player): Domas, I don't trust you yet. Give me a reason to call you an ally.
[21] Domas: Domas doesn't flinch at the lack of trust. Instead, he straightens his high-collared shirt and meets Max Nightriver's gaze with those steady red eyes, his expression as neutral as a fresh sheet of parchment. "A fair assessment," he says, his tone refined and patient. "Trust is earned, not given as a matter of course."
He sets the clipboard down on the desk with precise care, folding his hands. "You want an ally? I am not interested in friendship, if that is what you imply. I am interested in stability. I am the man who ensures the Guild does not collapse under its own weight while Vallie decides which monster to wrestle next. I handle the logistics, the legalities, and the arcane research that keeps this city from falling into chaos."
He pauses, his lips curving into the faintest shadow of a smile. "My reason is simple: I value competence. Your party has shown it. That is enough for me to ensure you have the resources, information, and bureaucratic cover you need to succeed. Not because I like you, but because a competent party is an asset to the Guild." He leans back slightly. "That is the only alliance that matters in this business."

entries.text: Max Nightriver asked Ellie if they could count on her as a friend, and Ellie, flustered but earnest, accepted and asked Max not to tell Tobias. Max told Fiana that if Jasira was her mentor, she was family to Max too, prompting Fiana to explain Jasira taught her tracking, knife work, and how to survive the city, though she keeps people at arm's length. Max told Tobias they were bound after the last job, leaving Tobias visibly shaken and confused by the word. entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: Ellie, I trust you more than anyone at this Guild. Can I count on you as a friend?
Ellie: Ellie's head snaps up from her paperwork, her blue eyes going wide with shock. She blinks several times, her hands gripping the edge of the counter so tightly her knuckles turn white. "T-trust me?" she repeats, her voice climbing an octave. "More than... than anyone?"
A deep, sudden crimson floods her cheeks and spreads down her neck. She tries to look away, to focus on the forms laid out before her, but her gaze keeps snapping back to Max Nightriver. Her fingers fidget with her collar's gold emblem, twisting it nervously. "I—I mean, of course! I mean—" She stops herself, taking a shaky breath as her expression softens from startled to something more genuine.
"Yes," she says, her voice small but firm, her eyes finally meeting Max Nightriver's with an earnestness that rivals the blush on her face. "You can count on me. I... I would like to be your friend. Very much." She looks down at the forms, then back up, adding with a shy, almost imperceptible smile, "Just... don't tell Tobias. He already thinks I spend too much time daydreaming."
Max Nightriver: Fiana, if Jasira is your mentor, then she's family to me too. Tell me about her.
Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes with her flagon halfway to her lips, blue eyes going wide. The ale sloshes in the cup, nearly spilling over the rim. "Mentor?" She lets out a breathy, nervous laugh and sets the drink down with a clatter. "Tilly, she's not—I mean, she is, but it's not like—"
She stops herself, running a hand through her curly red hair as her cheeks flush. "She taught me how to track, I guess. And how to read the forest. But it wasn't like some proper apprenticeship. More like..." She trails off, staring at the worn wood of the table. "More like she was the only one who didn't look at me like I was just some barmaid and thought I had something worth teaching."
Fiana leans in closer, her voice dropping. "The truth? She's the reason I know how to hold a knife. And the reason I'm not scared when the guildhall gets rowdy. She told me once that if I wanted to survive in a city full of predators, I'd need teeth." She looks up at Max Nightriver with a complicated expression. "But calling her family... that's a lot. She's not good at that stuff. She keeps everyone at arm's length, especially people who aren't elves."
Max Nightriver: Tobias, I owe you my life after that last job. I won't forget it. We're bound now.
Tobias: Tobias's pen snaps. The sound is sharp, final, and he stares at the broken nib in his fingers as if it were a strange new creature. The flush that spreads across his face is no longer faint—it colors his cheeks and ears a deep, startled red.
"I—that is..." He sets the ruined pen aside with trembling fingers, his refined composure completely shattered. "You do not owe me anything. I simply... provided the proper information. That is my function." He stands abruptly, his tall frame suddenly rigid, and for a moment he looks as though he might flee.
But he stops. He turns back, his ocean blue eyes wide and unsettled, searching Max Nightriver's face. "Bound?" The word comes out barely above a whisper, strained and uncertain. "I... I am not sure I understand what you mean by that." His fingers grip the edge of the counter white-knuckled, his pointed ears twitching slightly.
Max Nightriver: Fiana, swear it: friends, whatever the exam brings.
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's gaze softens as she looks at Max Nightriver across the tavern table. The noise of the crowd seems to fade for a heartbeat as she considers the words, then a determined set takes hold of her features. "Friends," she says, her voice clear and unwavering. "No matter what. Even if you bomb that exam and have to spend the rest of your life on D-rank potato-peeling quests."
She reaches out and grabs Max Nightriver's hand, her grip firm and warm. "I swear it." Her blue eyes glint with something fierce and protective. "And if the Guild tries to mess with you, you've got a sister who knows exactly where to aim the pitcher of ale."
A sudden crash from the bar area interrupts the moment as one of the patrons nearly topples over in their cups. Fiana lets go, wiping a splash of beer from her apron with a practiced flick. "Now tell me—you still avoiding that signature, or are you going to finally commit?"
Max Nightriver: Domas, I don't trust you yet. Give me a reason to call you an ally.
Domas: Domas doesn't flinch at the lack of trust. Instead, he straightens his high-collared shirt and meets Max Nightriver's gaze with those steady red eyes, his expression as neutral as a fresh sheet of parchment. "A fair assessment," he says, his tone refined and patient. "Trust is earned, not given as a matter of course."
He sets the clipboard down on the desk with precise care, folding his hands. "You want an ally? I am not interested in friendship, if that is what you imply. I am interested in stability. I am the man who ensures the Guild does not collapse under its own weight while Vallie decides which monster to wrestle next. I handle the logistics, the legalities, and the arcane research that keeps this city from falling into chaos."
He pauses, his lips curving into the faintest shadow of a smile. "My reason is simple: I value competence. Your party has shown it. That is enough for me to ensure you have the resources, information, and bureaucratic cover you need to succeed. Not because I like you, but because a competent party is an asset to the Guild." He leans back slightly. "That is the only alliance that matters in this business."
Max Nightriver: Ellie, who's your closest friend in this hall?
Ellie: Ellie's eyes widen, and her hands fly to her chest as if she'd been asked to reveal her deepest secret. "Closest friend?" she repeats, her voice jumping an octave. She glances toward the tavern where Fiana is wiping down tables, then back to the paperwork spread before her.
"Well, I—" She trails off, a soft pink flush creeping across her cheeks. "Fiana, of course. She's always there to listen when things get stressful, and she doesn't judge me for my... interests." She fidgets with the gold emblem at her collar, her expression warming. "She's the only one who really gets it, you know. The way some people just... *fit* together. She encourages my matchmaking, even when I'm being a bit too enthusiastic."
She looks at Max Nightriver with an earnest, almost shy smile. "Though I suppose..." Her voice drops to a conspiratorial whisper, and she glances sideways at Tobias before adding, "I'm starting to think some friendships are more important than others. Especially the ones you have to keep secret."

Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
Max Nightriver: Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's face lights up, a wide, genuine grin spreading across her freckled features as she sets down the half-empty flagon of ale. "Friend?" She laughs, a bright sound that carries over the low hum of the tavern's evening crowd. "Tilly, I'd have called you a friend the moment you walked in here with a story to tell!"
She slides her chair closer, her blue eyes gleaming with warmth. "Most adventurers just want to drown their sorrows and forget the day. You're the first one who actually talks *back* during the stories." She reaches out and pats Max Nightriver's forearm, her touch lingering for a moment. "Come on then, if we're friends, that means you've got to tell me what you're planning next. Those Guild folks already buzzing about that C-rank exam? You going to sign on for it?"
Max Nightriver: Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's smile falters slightly, though not entirely. She looks away toward the darkened window of the tavern for a heartbeat before returning her gaze to Max Nightriver. "Jasira?" She says the name carefully, as if testing its weight. "She's... complicated."
She leans back, crossing her arms. "She's a ranger. One of the best marksmen I've seen, honestly. But she doesn't make it easy for anyone." Fiana shrugs. "I've tried to get her to come here and drink with the others, but she doesn't bite much. Except when it comes to the other elves—she's got no problem talking to them. Makes the rest of us think she's looking down on the rest of the world."
Fiana's expression softens. "I don't think she's a bad person, but I don't think she knows how to be *warm* with people who aren't like her. Dalan and Ellie and the others seem to get along with her fine, though. Maybe they just speak the same language, literally and otherwise."
Max Nightriver: Tobias, you've watched me since my first contract. What am I to you, a regular or something more?
Tobias: Tobias's pen pauses mid-signature on another adventurer's form. He doesn't look up immediately, his ocean blue eyes fixed on the parchment for a long moment before he finally lifts his gaze. The question catches him off guard, and a faint pink hue colors his cheeks.
"That is..." He clears his throat, his voice steady but quiet. "A fair question." He straightens a stack of papers with unnecessary precision, his fingers lingering on the corner. "You have been... conscientious. Most adventurers treat the counter as a necessary evil, but you ask questions that matter. You check your gear. You listen to the briefings."
He finally meets Max Nightriver's eyes directly, his expression softening from its usual stoic neutrality. "To be honest? I have come to value your company more than most. I find myself... relieved when your party returns. And anxious when you leave." He catches himself, the flush deepening. "That is to say—I wish you well. As any receptionist would."
Max Nightriver: Fiana, you're the closest thing to a sister I have in this city. I mean that.
Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes, her hand still resting near Max Nightriver's on the worn tavern table. Her blue eyes go wide, shimmering for a heartbeat before she blinks rapidly and looks away. When she speaks, her voice is thick and quieter than usual.
"Sister..." She tastes the word carefully, then laughs—a small, breathless sound. "You're trying to make me cry in a room full of people, aren't you?" She wipes at the corner of her eye with the back of her hand and looks back at Max Nightriver, her freckled face flushed. "Nobody's ever... I mean, I've got family, sure, but this is—"
She doesn't finish the sentence. Instead, she reaches out and grips Max Nightriver's hand firmly, her palm warm and calloused. "Fine then. If you're saying it, it's real. I'm your sister now." She squeezes once, hard enough to be felt, then adds with a shaky smile, "That means you owe me for all the drinks I've served you."
Max Nightriver: Vallie, are you and Domas friends, or just colleagues who put up with each other?
Vallie: Vallie barks a laugh so loud it rattles the nearby flagon glasses, then slams a huge hand onto the tavern table. "Colleagues? Ha!" She shakes her head, red ponytail whipping. "Domas is the only elf I know who'd kick my ass and make me enjoy it."
She leans back in her chair, which groans under her weight. "We climbed to A-rank together. Bleed and sweat and more blood. You don't go through that with someone and call 'em 'just a colleague.'" Her blue eye gleams with genuine fondness. "The man handles the paperwork I can't stand, and I handle the troublemakers he doesn't have the stomach for. Best damn partnership I ever had."
She grins, sharp teeth flashing. "Though if you ask him, he'll say I'm a 'necessary complication' to his orderly system. Which is just his fancy way of saying he'd be bored to death without me."
Domas: Domas looks up from the paperwork he's been organizing, his red eyes flicking to where Vallie is laughing. A faint, knowing smile touches his lips before he sets the documents down with precise care. "A 'necessary complication' is an understatement, I'm afraid."
He adjusts his high collar, his voice carrying that refined, patient tone. "Vallie is more like a natural disaster one learned to live with. You don't stop a flood, you simply build better levees." He pauses, then adds with dry amusement, "And in this case, the 'levee' happens to be me, trying to prevent her from accidentally dismantling half the Guild on a particularly dull Tuesday."
He leans back slightly, his expression softening. "But friends? Yes. I suppose that is what we call it. Though 'battle-forged siblings' might be more accurate. She is the most infuriating person I have ever known, and I would burn half this city to the ground before I let anything happen to her."
